Hi Alex / Priya —

Following up with more specifics on the items you asked about. High-level recommendations based on what we’ve seen across similar migrations: 

Vector dimensions
- For highest general-purpose text similarity we recommend 1536-dimensional embeddings (e.g., text-embed-3-large equivalent). They hit a good balance for semantic nuance and retrieval quality.
- 768 dims (smaller models) are acceptable for coarse semantic filtering and reduce storage/cost ~2x; choose if your top concerns are cost and index size.

Batching & throughput
- Reindexing (offline): aim for batch sizes 512–2048 depending on memory. With a 64-core / 512GB machine you should be able to use 1024+ batches when using float16 generation and streaming writes to the vector DB.
- Real-time generation (server-side): default 64–256 per request batching is a pragmatic starting point. If you have bursty bulk-ingestion, use an async worker pool to build batches up to 512 before calling the embed endpoint.
- Monitor per-request latency & tokenization overhead; Redwood’s SDK exposes a batch/bytes estimator to help pick a sweet spot.

Normalization & similarity metric
- We recommend unit-normalizing (L2 normalize to unit length) vectors at ingestion if you plan to use cosine similarity. Normalizing at ingest standardizes storage and makes per-query costs predictable.
- If you cannot normalize at ingest (e.g., legacy constraints), you can normalize at query time, but this increases CPU at query and can complicate hybrid pipelines.

Reranking strategy
- Two-stage: dense retrieval (ANN) for recall -> cross-encoder rerank for precision works best.
- Typical pattern: retrieve top-200 with ANN, re-rank top-10–50 with the cross-encoder depending on latency SLOs. Top-10 is common for UI search; top-50 for recommendation systems where downstream cost is acceptable.
- Redwood supports structured rerank outputs (score + labels + span offsets) so the cross-encoder can return JSON-like structured results for downstream UI highlighting or tool calling.

Migration approach (practical steps)
1) Snapshot current index and sample-quality check: export 1–5% of documents, run A/B comparisons (current vs Redwood embeddings + retriever) on your key queries.
2) Versioned reindex: create a new index namespace (e.g., acme_v2_202705) and write embeddings there. Don’t delete old index until quality & perf checks pass.
3) Dual-run traffic: route a % of production reads to the new index (5–20%) to compare behavior in prod.
4) Final cutover and old index decommission after 2–4 weeks of stable metrics.

Storage & datatype notes
- Use float32 for storage if you need maximum fidelity; float16 is usually fine and halves storage. Redwood’s SDK can output float16 and offer checksums to validate reindex fidelity.
- If you use FAISS/HNSW, remember to tune M/efConstruction for your expected throughput.

Other tips
- Keep embedding model versioning in metadata (embedding_model: text-embed-3-large_v1) so you can roll back or compare.
- Add a lightweight sampling eval job run weekly to catch regressions early.

Happy to walk through a migration runbook during the deep-dive — we can share a checklist and sample scripts.
